w: Founded in 1936 by Caltech rocket researchers, later folded into NASA, JPL builds the solar system's robotic explorers: Curiosity, Perseverance, the Juno probe at Jupiter. It runs the Deep Space Network tracking craft beyond the Moon; its Space Flight Operations Facility is a National Historic Landmark.
s: NASA's planet-hopping lab, born from a rocket club
_facts: Founded 1936 by Caltech researchers
Now owned by NASA, managed by Caltech
Builds/operates Curiosity, Perseverance, Juno, Psyche missions
Space Flight Operations Facility is a National Historic Landmark

w: Frank Lloyd Wright's La Miniatura, built 1924 for rare-book dealer Alice Millard, was the first of his four concrete 'textile block' houses in Los Angeles. It sits over an arroyo ravine with two entrances a storey apart: pedestrians enter below, cars above. On the National Register.
s: Wright's textile-block house over an arroyo ravine
_facts: Built 1924 for Alice Millard, Wright's second house for her family
First of Wright's four LA concrete textile-block houses
Two entrances a storey apart: pedestrian below, vehicular above
On the National Register of Historic Places

w: Norton Simon amassed European paintings and tapestries alongside Asian bronzes and woodblock prints behind a brown-tile facade on the Rose Parade route, so its exterior turns up in every New Year broadcast. Rodin bronzes ring the entrance; more sculpture circles a pond out back.
s: Rodin out front, the Rose Parade route out the window
_facts: Formerly the Pasadena Art Institute/Art Museum
Holds European and Asian art: paintings, sculpture, tapestries, woodblock prints
Rodin sculptures at the entrance, more around a pond garden
Sits on Colorado Boulevard along the Rose Parade route

w: A concrete arch bridge spanning the Arroyo Seco, popularly nicknamed Suicide Bridge for the high number of suicides once committed here. Locals also call it simply Pasadena Bridge. Its dramatic curved span over the ravine has made it one of the city's most recognizable landmarks, and one of its most somber.
s: The 'Suicide Bridge' arcing over Arroyo Seco
_facts: Historic concrete arch bridge over the Arroyo Seco
Nicknamed Suicide Bridge for its history of suicides
Also known simply as Pasadena Bridge

w: Completed in 1927, Pasadena City Hall blends Mediterranean Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival architecture, prized as a significant example of the 1920s City Beautiful movement. It remains the working seat of city government at the heart of the Civic Center district.
s: A 1927 showpiece of the City Beautiful era
_facts: Completed 1927
Combines Mediterranean Revival and Spanish Colonial Revival styles
A significant example of the 1920s City Beautiful movement

w: Built in 1887 in Highland Park, this ornately decorated Queen Anne Victorian has been called the most photographed house in Los Angeles. Named a Historic-Cultural Monument in 1966 and NRHP-listed in 1972, it was relocated in 1970 to the Heritage Square Museum, where it remains open.
s: LA's most-photographed house, moved to a museum
_facts: Built 1887, Queen Anne Victorian style
Called 'the most photographed house' in Los Angeles
Declared a Historic-Cultural Monument 1966, NRHP-listed 1972
Relocated 1970 to the Heritage Square Museum

w: Also known as El Alisal ('alder grove' in Spanish), this Rustic Craftsman stone house was built by Charles Fletcher Lummis himself across the late 1800s and early 1900s, on the edge of the Arroyo Seco. A City Historic-Cultural Monument and National Register listee.
s: Lummis's hand-built stone house on the Arroyo Seco
_facts: Built by Charles Fletcher Lummis, late 19th-early 20th century
Name means 'alder grove' in Spanish
Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places

w: One of the world's largest and oldest cactus and succulent collections, assembled from expeditions across the Americas by Henry Huntington and curator William Hertrich. Part of the Huntington Library's grounds, it gathers extreme-climate plants from deserts worldwide.
s: One of the world's oldest cactus collections
_facts: Part of the Huntington Library, Art Collections and Botanical Gardens
One of the world's largest/oldest cacti and succulent collections
Built from plants Henry Huntington and William Hertrich gathered across the Americas

w: Founded in 1771 as the fourth of California's twenty-one missions, its stone church was built with capped buttresses and narrow windows unique among the missions. Legend holds a painting of Our Lady of Sorrows won over Tongva resistance to its founding. Its cemetery holds some 6,000 neophytes.
s: A 1771 mission, its cemetery holding 6,000 souls
_facts: Founded September 8, 1771, the 4th of 21 California missions
Designed by Antonio Cruzado; unique capped buttresses, narrow windows
Campo Santo cemetery holds roughly 6,000 neophytes
Legend: a painting of Our Lady of Sorrows won Tongva acceptance of the mission

w: A 686-seat auditorium at 39 South El Molino Avenue, the Pasadena Playhouse stages professional shows alongside cultural events and community programs throughout the year, making it one of the city's principal performing-arts venues.
s: A 686-seat stage on El Molino Avenue
_facts: 686-seat auditorium at 39 S. El Molino Avenue
Hosts professional shows, cultural events, community engagements

w: An open-air architecture museum beside the Arroyo Seco Parkway, gathering relocated historic buildings, including the Hale House, to trace a century of Los Angeles growth from 1850 to 1950. Volunteer interpreters lead tours weaving together the history, architecture and culture of the region's boom years.
s: Rescued historic houses, moved and reassembled
_facts: Open-air living history and architecture museum
Located beside the Arroyo Seco Parkway in Montecito Heights
Interprets Los Angeles history and architecture, 1850-1950
Received the relocated 1887 Hale House in 1970

w: The only institution dedicated to Pasadena and the west San Gabriel Valley's history, headquartered on the century-old Fenyes Estate. Its grounds hold the estate gardens, a research library and archives, the Curtin House and the Finnish Folk Art Museum, hosting exhibits, tours and lectures on the region's past.
s: Pasadena's history, kept on a century-old estate
_facts: The only institution devoted to Pasadena/west San Gabriel Valley history
Headquartered on the historic Fenyes Estate
Includes the Curtin House and the Finnish Folk Art Museum
Nonprofit museum, research library and archives
